To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
openQ*D-0.1 is a versatile tool for lattice QCD and QCD+QETD simulations.
openQ*D is a versatile and efficient code for QCD+QE and QCD simulations with and without $$C^*$$ boundary condition, with O(a) improved fermions and with a wide variety of gauge ensembles.
we have developed openQ*D- 1.0, a new open-source package for lattice simulations of QED+QCD and QCD.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the strong interaction, which is described by Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD), and the electromagnetic interaction, which is governed by Quantum Electrodynamics (QED).
the development and implementation of algorithms for lattice gauge theory, in particular for QCD+ QED.
the development of numerical tools for lattice simulations of gauge theories, and in particular of QCD+U(1) QED and QCD with dynamical fermions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
openQ*D-2.1 is a very useful tool for lattice QCD simulations.
the openQ*D code has the same features and performance as its predecessors, but it also provides new functionalities, which we will describe in the following sections.
openQ*D provides a versatile tool to perform QCD+QCD simulations in the presence of dynamical photons, and it is a powerful tool to study the physics of QED in the non-perturbative regime.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

openQ*D-0.9.2 has been used to produce the first lattice QCD+QCD simulations with $$\mathrm {O} (a)$$-improved Wilson fermions and $$\mathrm {N_f}=2$$, $$\mathrm {T}=2$$, and $$\mathrm N_c$$=3, and the results have been used to calculate hadronic observables in the continuum limit.

we have developed a code which allows us to simulate QCD+QET with $$\mathrm {O}(a)$$-improved Wilson fermions in the continuum limit with $$\mathrm{C}^* \times \mathrm{C}$$ boundary conditions, with an emphasis on the study of isospin-breaking effects in the light hadron spectrum.
the openQ*D code provides a flexible and powerful tool for QCD and QCD+QEd simulations, with a wide range of applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the openQ*D code can be used as a generic framework to simulate QCD-like theories with Wilson fermions, and can be adapted to any lattice discretization, including the one of the openQCD-2.0 project (openQCD-2 project. http://www.openQCD.org, 2020).
the openQ*D package can be used as a versatile tool for lattice QCD+QCD simulations, as we have demonstrated by successfully running several benchmark simulations.

openQ*D- 1.0 is a versatile code, which can also be used to perform simulations of pure QCD with Wilson fermions, with or without $$\mathrm{C}^*_{\rm s}$$ boundary conditions, with the same accuracy and performance as openQCD.
